observations: Photo 0 is the only photo and it is very dark.
It shows the side and bulging rear housing of a tube (CRT) television with vent slots, standing on a terrazzo floor; the front bezel edge is at the right.
The screen is not visible and the TV is not shown powered on.
No brand, logo, model label or screen size can be read anywhere in photo 0.
A cable runs over the rear housing; no remote or accessories are shown.

identity.kind: faulty CRT tube TV, not working, for parts

claims.evidence: Photo 0 is too dark and shows no logo, label or screen; brand and size cannot be read.

claims.claim: The transformer got blown (TV is faulty)
claims.evidence: No photo of the screen or a power-on attempt; taken at the seller's word against interest and priced as not working.
The seller's own words say the transformer is blown.
Photo 0 is too dark to show the cabinet or screen condition.
Internal history cannot be seen; a blown transformer suggests it may already have been opened.
No receipt or warranty shown; implausible for an old tube TV.

risks.risk: Fault is wider than the transformer: dead tube, burnt main board or cracked picture tube
risks.proof: Clip of the TV plugged in and switched on, showing what happens on the screen
risks.if_unproven: as dead, for parts or scrap only

risks.risk: Screen size smaller than the claimed 29 inch
risks.proof: Daylight photo of the full front with a tape measure across the screen diagonal
risks.if_unproven: at the smallest common tube TV size

risks.risk: Cracked screen or broken cabinet hidden by the dark photo
risks.proof: Clear daylight photos of the front screen and all sides
Close-up of the rating label on the back cover

proof_requests: Clear daylight photo of the whole front of the TV including the screen
Close-up of the rating label on the back showing brand, model and size
Clip of the TV plugged in and switched on
Photo with a tape measure across the screen diagonal
response.reason: The photo shows a tube TV and the seller says it is faulty, so it is priced at its worst case as a non-working CRT TV for parts, of unread brand and size; the 'works perfectly' claim is contradicted by the seller's own words.
